survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS) and therefore does not define a sampling frame, student-level analytic dataset, or any survey-weight variables. The document describes governance roles and expenditure shares across national, regional (autonomous regions), and local levels in Portugal’s adult skills system. As a result, there are no plausible values (PV) or scaling procedures, and no complex survey design features to weight. If analysts were to conduct an empirical ILSA-based study on adult skills outcomes, they would need to use the relevant ILSA sampling weights (and replicate weights if provided) from the microdata; this note itself provides none.

Similarly, missing data handling is not reported because no microdata are analyzed.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note provides a descriptive overview of how Portugal’s adult skills system is governed across national, regional (autonomous regions of Madeira and the Azores), and local levels (municipalities and sub-municipal parishes). It reports the share of general government expenditure at the subnational level (13.6%) and summarizes which policy areas are set, funded, implemented, and delivered at each governance level (VET, HVET, CET, adult education/AE, and ALMPs). The note explains that governance is relatively centralised: the national government sets the legislative framework and strategy, while direct delivery occurs locally, with autonomous regions holding additional competencies. It also details key institutions (e.g., IEFP, ANQEP) and how social partners participate as providers and in agencies. No student assessment data, sampling design, scaling, or PV-based benchmarks are analyzed in this document.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical large-scale assessment study; it is a policy/governance country note compiled by the OECD. Consequently, there is no ILSA cycle, grade, domain, or student-level outcome to model, and fields such as sample size, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are structurally absent by design. The extraction therefore focuses on governance responsibilities and institutional roles rather than statistical results.
